generations.prompt: Repaint the first image as a square transparent game effects atlas with EXACTLY four equal cells, 2 columns by 2 rows, preserving the centered positions and relative extents in each cell. PRIMARY style reference Giovanni da Modena's Inferno in Bologna, second and third references, match the broad ochre/iron-red/umber pigment and decisive brown outlines of the demon in the fourth reference. These are painted punishments from a medieval infernal wall, not magical VFX. TOP LEFT: a circular band of 12-16 sharp simple medieval flame tongues, charred almost-black base, iron red and ochre bodies, narrow opaque bone-white tips. Large empty transparent center. The fire is graphic and flat with separated deliberately drawn tongues, NO realistic turbulent flames or sparks. TOP RIGHT: a quiet warning boundary, a plain circular scar in dirty bone and graphite plaster with 8 blunt chips, dark brown underpaint, absolutely no glyphs, stars, runes, ornaments or invented seal. Large transparent center. BOTTOM LEFT: one broad upward-arching crescent of exactly five hooked tongues of infernal fire, strong brown-black outline and flat iron red planes, ochre inside and limited bone on the edge, not a smooth speed smear. BOTTOM RIGHT: a broad horizontal jagged cracked plaster fissure, dirty bone lips over a narrow almost black interior, a few restrained iron-red shadows, hand-drawn coarse flat forms; no light emission. Every cell has clear empty gutters. Tempera, a few broad dry-brush marks, selective lime losses, strong readable silhouette at small size. No 3D volume, no soft gradients, no bloom, no gold jewelry, no lens flare, no particle dust, no digitally glowing white core. Bright bone is opaque pigment against dark contours. Transparent background, no text, no grid lines.

Repaint the supplied game effect sprite sheet completely in the flat medieval fresco technique of the supplied Giovanni da Modena Inferno in Bologna, the PRIMARY style reference. Output a transparent square atlas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, sixteen separate sprites, generous transparent gutters, no labels or frames. Each row is four distinct hand-painted animation cels. Broad confident dark umber outlines, flat large planes of bone white, ochre, iron red, umber and cool slate. Very little small detail; occasional broad scraped plaster chips, no uniformly speckled noise. NO digital glow, halos, realistic smoke, bloom, gradients, glossy objects, decorative fantasy runes or seals. Row 1: four successive cels of an opening little jagged wound in plaster, pale hand of a damned soul and crow feather struggling out of a dark crack; modest contained silhouette, grows only through the drawn cels. Row 2: four horizontal rightwards flying hooked tongues of medieval fire, like sharp flames painted around the devils in the reference; a pale pointed bone core, opaque black-red contour, three swept flames not smooth motion trails. Row 3: four top-down circular ground-warning boundaries: very clear plain bone-white circle outlined in near-black umber, slightly chipped plaster edges, tiny inward slate fissures. Keep the circle identical diameter throughout; empty transparent centre. These are unlettered boundaries NOT occult symbols, NO stars, spikes or invented sigils. Row 4: four successive cels of a vertical rupture in the wall of Hell: first a simple crooked white plaster split framed by slate, second broad split exposing one small anguished pale face and two hands, third large bone/slate fallen angular slabs, fourth a few heavy plaster shards. This is a painted crack in the fresco, NOT an electric discharge or lightning glow. Entire artwork flat and forceful like the reference's broad rock planes and naked pale bodies. All sixteen cells cleanly isolated, equal 4x4 grid, centred in each cell.

Repaint this game ground-effects atlas entirely as a medieval painted fresco in the style of Giovanni da Modena Inferno, San Petronio Bologna shown in references 2 and 3. Transparent wide canvas with exactly FOUR columns TWO rows, eight isolated top-down circular effect sprites, each centred in its own equal square cell, all same outer diameter, clear gutters. These are flat paintings laid on the floor, not perspective scenes. Primary palette: broad umber/iron-red/ochre/dirty bone/slate areas with thick dark-brown brush contour. Simplify greatly, decisive large shapes, just a few plaster chips. NO glow, no bloom, no realistic rendered smoke or bubbles, no evenly noisy microdetail, no digital highlights, no decorative glyphs. TOP ROW four animation cels of hellfire: 1 cold black-red cracked plaster around a small painted ember; 2 five sharp angular medieval flame tongues, iron red filled with ochre and bone cores, rising out of black crack; 3 same site with flames bent differently, two tiny pale hands reaching from between flames; 4 angular ash fragments and dull bone scars after the fire. The outlines of the circular site stay fixed. BOTTOM ROW four cels of Buer's poison: 1 sickly ochre and olive-grey plaster wound with black-root cracks; 2 a flat murky black-olive pool with two pale clawing damned hands and a simple contorted face, thick sweeping bile strokes not realistic liquid; 3 same pool with hands shifted and big ochre ripples / thorn roots; 4 dead bone-grey root shards and olive residue. Restrained green pigment, never acid neon. Each of eight sprites has a transparent background with irregular chipped perimeter, no painted rectangular backing. The circles occupy about 88 percent of cell width; no overlap between cells. Broad simple forms readable when tiny in game, like the rocks, flames and damned bodies painted on the reference wall.

Repaint the supplied sixteen-sprite game impact atlas as flat medieval tempera on chipped plaster, primary reference Giovanni da Modena Inferno (Bologna) supplied. Transparent square, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells with generous clear gutters, no labels. Each row is an impact animation sequence of four different hand-painted cels: 1 small initial impact, 2 decisive large burst, 3 dispersal, 4 a few falling pieces. Row 1: angular fragments of limestone, umber contours, flat broad bone and slate planes, maximum 8 large chips in any cel, no fine powder. Row 2: blood in broad irregular iron-red brush strokes, dark brown contour and deep burgundy underside, like pigments flung from a fresco brush, not realistic watery droplets, never glossy. Row 3: thick flat ochre/umber plaster dust shapes and 4 large chips, shape like a scraped-off section of a painted wall, NOT volumetric smoke. Row 4: gunpowder detonation in medieval Hell: sharp irregular black-red flame tongues with bone-white and ochre cores and 5 flying plaster chips, at the heart of second cel a tiny bleak face glimpsed in the wall crack. Expanding only through the drawn cels then leaving dark plaster fragments. No electricity, stars, sparkles or lens flare. Broad dark sinopia drawing, confident simple shapes, uneven modest plaster scars, low detail. Palette very restricted bone, ochre, iron red, umber, slate. No smooth shading, glow, bloom, neon, photographic realism, 3D rendering, uniform speckle, decorative glyphs or seals. All sprites stay entirely inside their own cells on genuinely transparent background. The game must feel like the Inferno fresco came alive.

Repaint all eight icons from the first reference as a flat medieval fresco atlas, using Giovanni da Modena Inferno (second reference) as PRIMARY stylistic guide. Repaint these two architectural texture images as confident flat medieval fresco surfaces in the technique of the supplied Giovanni da Modena Inferno, primary reference. LEFT square preserves first reference's exact 2x2 texture layout: top-left pale bone limestone blocks, top-right slate-grey limestone blocks, bottom-left plain iron-red painted plaster, bottom-right a 4x4 checker of bone/red/slate floor tiles.
